No pretty sure our fork choice will pick EMPTY but might cause issues with stf Lodestar picked empty. stf was fine does your bid commit to an empty `execution_requests_root`? Yes. Quoting my llm > 0x87b69a306c8e430d0857f7c4ac5e27cecffa1108d43c2e5df7388056fea7a423 > > That is the SSZ root of an ExecutionRequests object whose request lists are empty—it is not the all-zero hash. > > Why: Buildoor first constructs an ordinary payload with no deposits, withdrawals, consolidations, builder deposits, or builder exits. The attack transformation changes only: > > bid.block_hash = bid.parent_block_hash > > and then re-signs the bid. It deliberately preserves the genuine empty-requests commitment. but so lodestar should be doing fine? I don't know why I keep getting these warnings 😅 It does not render the text, just says duplicate although I am pretty sure message is not an exact dup anyway, lodestar stalls later on because of sync distance being high that in turn is because 2/3 validators (LH + Teku) miss their proposals because they are stuck with an unresolvable FULL parent whose exec block hash the malicious builder aliased in their bid yeah but that you can work around, however, the empty slot is misclassified as full since we run `apply_parent_execution_payload` Aha, interesting. so stf breaks because of the hash alias even though parent is initially classified as empty ``` Sep-02 13:32:56.501[api] error: Block production failed slot=34, parentSlot=29, parentBlockRoot=0x047a649c3751506a73c4ff0028c0784f0192227305586660afa3484f74146f36, parentBlockHash=0xd431b263c3eb10ae09c4dd66034dd2b54ea51a65b1a726f13fbdd3ad27cc313c, fork=gloas, builderBoostFactor=90, strictFeeRecipientCheck=false, circuitBreakerActive=false, builderEntries=0, engineReason=Error: Parent execution requests root mismatch actual=0x87b69a306c8e430d0857f7c4ac5e27cecffa1108d43c2e5df7388056fea7a423 expected=0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff, bidReason=Error: No builder bid available Sep-02 13:32:56.502[rest] error: Req req-l5 produceBlockV4 error - excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content:
Yes. Quoting my llm

> 0x87b69a306c8e430d0857f7c4ac5e27cecffa1108d43c2e5df7388056fea7a423
> 
>   That is the SSZ root of an ExecutionRequests object whose request lists are empty—it is not the all-zero hash.
> 
>   Why: Buildoor first constructs an ordinary payload with no deposits, withdrawals, consolidations, builder deposits, or builder exits. The attack transformation changes only:
> 
>   bid.block_hash = bid.parent_block_hash
> 
>   and then re-signs the bid. It deliberately preserves the genuine empty-requests commitment.
